newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aerospatiale swings back to profit.
newsitem.headline: Aerospatiale swings back to profit.

text.p: French state-owned Aerospatiale Friday reported a return to profit for 1996, with a recovery in civilian aircraft markets allowing it to avoid restructuring charges which had previously tipped it into loss.

The group, due to be taken private by combat plane maker Dassault Aviation this year, posted a net profit after payment to minority shareholders of 812 million French francs ($140 million). In 1995, it lost 981 million, including 1.4 billion ($242.3 million) in restructuring charges.
"The results for the 1997 year should...see a very significant turn in the group's profitability, allowing a doubling of profits," Aerospatiale said in a statement.
Aerospatiale makes parts and assembles passenger jets for the Airbus Industrie consortium, and also manufactures tactical and strategic missiles, satellites and helicopters.

Sales this year are expected to rise to 60 billion francs ($10.4 million) from 50.9 billion francs ($8.8 million), helped by increased aircraft sales to Airbus, cost-cutting measures and the rise in the dollar. It expects to deliver 190 Airbus jets, up from 126 in 1996.

"The major difference between 1995 and 1996 comes basically from the fact we had high restructuring charges in 1995. The recovery in business means we do not need new provisions in 1996," Chairman Yves Michot told a news conference.

Aerospatiale's operating profit rose 15 percent to 736 million francs ($127.4 million) from 639 million ($110.6 million) a year ago. Its share in the Airbus consortium provided by far the biggest earnings contribution, with 1.175 billion francs ($203.4 million), vs. 1.075 billion ($186.1 million) in 1995.

Aerospatiale owns 38 percent of Airbus, the same share as Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa). British Aerospace Plc (BAe) owns 20 percent, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain holds 4 percent.

The helicopter business, held through a 70 percent stake in the Eurocopter joint venture with Dasa, hurt Aerospatiale's results to the tune of 224 million francs ($38.8 million), but was lower than the 817 million franc ($141.4 million) hit taken in 1995.

After a 1996 loss expected to be around 300 million ($51.9 million), Eurocopter's prospects should improve with 11.8 billion francs ($2.0 million) of new orders booked last year vs. 6.8 billion ($1.2 million) in 1995.
Space and defence activities contributed 206 million francs ($35.7 million) to operating profit, down from 412 million ($71.3 million).
Other aeronautical activities ran a loss of 314 million francs ($54.4 million) vs. a 156 million ($27.0 million) loss in 1995, mainly due to a mediocre market in aircraft maintenance.
